subject: qplot error: cannot coerce class '"times"' into a data.frame

messages.author: 6cfe1f2fd7c7f663
messages.subject: qplot error: cannot coerce class '"times"' into a data.frame
parts:
I'm going through Hadley Wickham's ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis and am trying to apply the examples to my own data after running through the example data.

I have a data frame dallas with three columns. The column offense_time contains times objects from the chron library.

Behind the scenes, the values are stored as floating point numbers between 0 and 1, where 0 = 0:00 midnight, 0.5 = 12 noon, and 0.999988425...  = 23:59:59.

For example, if I do this:

> d <- times("13:02:00")
> fix(d)

I get this:
structure(0.543055555555556, format = "h:m:s", class = "times")

I get this error:

> qplot(dallas$offense_time,data=dallas,geom="histogram",binwidth=1)
Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) : 
  cannot coerce class '"times"' into a data.frame

I tried to do some searching. I found some posts on this forum that are kind of related to this but don't answer the direct problem.

Is it possible to use items of class times with ggplot2?

Aren

Wait, aren't I already doing that already by following that stackoverflow method (link)?

Given a timestamp 1-7-2011 21:47, I am subtracting the POSIX value for midnight the same day, leaving the # of seconds that 21:47:00 is after midnight the same day.

In that case, my constant value for the date is zero, right?

So if my first time is 0 and last time is 23*60*60 + 59*60 + 59 = 86399, which makes sense because value 86400 would be the first second of the next day (0:00:00 1-2-1970).

messages.subject: Re: qplot error: cannot coerce class '"times"' into a data.frame
parts:
OK, there is an issue with time zone conversion with this method.

Where I live is CST (GMT -6). Posix 0 is not 0:00:00 1-1-1970, it's 18:00:00 12-31-1969. So I can't range from 0 to 86399; I have to range from 0+ 21600 to 86399+21600, which is 21600 to 107999. (21600 is the number of seconds in 6 hours.)

How do I tell ggplot2 to not attempt to convert for time zones?

Aren
